sections.h2: Who answers questions about an Orange County tax statement?
sections.html:
Orange County divides the job three ways, so the right call depends on the problem. A wrong value or missing exemption belongs to the Property Appraiser at 200 S Orange Ave, Suite 1700 in Orlando. A bill, a payment or a delinquency belongs to the Tax Collector. The rate itself is a product of local boards.

  • Value, ownership, legal description and mailing address: Property Appraiser.
  • Millage: the county commission, school board, cities and special districts.
  • Statements, payment plans, certificates: Tax Collector.

The Tax Collector distributes the money to 63 taxing authorities. Streetlights, sewers and road work are non-ad valorem charges, priced per unit and printed on the same statement.

The year's value is pinned to January 1. Statements reach owners by the first of November, and the balance must arrive at the Tax Collector before April begins.

Property tax dates in Orange County
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Last day to file an exemption request
AugustProposed tax notice mailed
By November 1Statements mailed
November to FebruaryFour, three, two and one percent discounts
March 31Gross amount and deferral applications due
April 1Delinquency begins
By June 1Online certificate sale

A check postmarked March 30 but delivered in April is late, because the office goes by receipt.

Pay in November and the bill drops four percent. Each later month trims one point less, ending at one percent in February, and March pays the gross figure.

Sellers who close in winter can pay the whole year at the closing table, so the month on the contract changes the net. Your title agent can quote the number for your actual closing day. When a lender escrows your taxes it may request the statement, and you receive a copy stamped with the lender's request. That copy does not call for a second payment.

Owners who are current and whose prior bill topped $100 can apply online at the Tax Collector's site for the quarterly installment plan.

sections.h2: Exemptions for an Orange County home
sections.html:
Homestead leads the list, and it can lower taxable value by as much as $50,000. The opening $25,000 touches every levy, and a second slice reaches only non-school levies above $50,000 of assessed value.

File with the Property Appraiser before March 1, and live in the house as your permanent home on January 1. Widow, disability, senior and military exemptions also exist. Once homesteaded, the assessed figure may rise each year by no more than the smaller of 3 percent or the inflation change. A sale wipes out that gap on the following January 1, so a buyer's first bill can be well above yours. The appraiser's tax estimator is aimed at people weighing a purchase or sale.

sections.h2: Can a house with old tax debt change hands?
sections.html:
You can still sell. The title agent requests a payoff from the Tax Collector, and every open balance gets cleared as part of closing.

Once April arrives, the Tax Collector adds a 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost. Parcels are listed in a local paper for three straight weeks, then certificates go up for competitive bids that start at 18 percent and drop. To clear a certificate, pay the tax, accrued interest and advertising cost. Late payers must use certified or cashier's funds, a money order, certain attorney, title or escrow checks, or cash at the counter. Personal and business checks are refused.

  • Ask for the payoff before you list.
  • Confirm whether a certificate already exists.
  • Compare escrow records with the county account.

sections.h2: How long before a certificate threatens the house?
sections.html:
Two years. Only then can the certificate holder apply for a tax deed, and Orange County routes those sales through the Comptroller's Office.

Before that, state law bars the holder from pressing the owner for payment. Homestead land gets one more cushion, because the opening bid must include half of its latest assessed value on top of the money due. An owner facing this stage should still call the Tax Collector's property tax department early and ask for a redemption total.

Qualifying homesteaders can postpone part of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector before April. This is a different program from the exemption.

Postponed tax remains a lien on the property. Before listing, ask the Tax Collector how a postponed balance, with interest, is paid off in a sale. The state ties the amount to household income and lets a permanent resident aged 65 or older defer the share above 3 percent of that income.

The appraiser's site offers a property search by address, owner name, sale history, property use and foreclosure status. It also links a tax estimator, a map site, downloadable forms, a tax roll and millage page, an income survey for commercial owners, code tables and a property fraud alert.

  • Use the search to confirm the parcel, owner and exemptions on your record.
  • Run the estimator when you want a buyer to see a likely tax picture.
  • Download the exemption forms if a new owner needs to file.
  • Sign up for the fraud alert to watch your record.

Treat the estimator as a planning aid, since a new owner may not keep the seller's exemptions.

A rental that holds furniture, fixtures or equipment can owe a second tax. The Tax Collector describes tangible personal property tax as a levy on those items in businesses and rental property, and on structural additions to mobile homes.

These statements arrive alongside the real estate statements and carry the same discounts. Past March 31 a monthly charge of 1.5 percent accrues, and a collection firm under contract adds 15 percent on accounts left unpaid. If you are selling a furnished rental, ask the Tax Collector how any open account is handled.

Orange County had 1,528,002 people in July 2025, spread over 527,776 households. Owners live in 56.8 percent of the homes, and the median value is $390,100. A median mortgage holder spends $2,055 monthly, against $1,775 for a typical rent.

A statement's lines shift with the home's location: inside a city, in unincorporated Orange County, or within a special district. Read those lines on your own account before quoting a tax figure to a buyer.

These are general steps for any seller. Confirm the owner name and exemptions on the parcel record. Ask the Tax Collector for a written payoff on any open year and for the redemption total if a certificate exists. Gather your latest statement and the August notice for the title agent. Agree in the contract on how the current year's tax is split, and read the settlement statement before you sign. A buyer paying cash can close faster, but open taxes are still paid from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Until what date can Orange County owners pay without a late charge?
faqs.a: March 31, counted by the day the Tax Collector receives it. A check that lands in April is delinquent.

faqs.q: What does a November payment save?
faqs.a: Four percent. The discount shrinks by a point each month until February, and March has none.

faqs.q: Which Orange County office fixes a wrong value or missing exemption?
faqs.a: The Property Appraiser. The Tax Collector bills what the certified roll shows and cannot change value, ownership or exemptions.

faqs.q: Can a homeowner with unpaid taxes still sell in Orange County?
faqs.a: Yes. Request the Tax Collector's payoff, then let the title agent settle it at closing, with certified funds if the bill is already delinquent.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate transfer my house to an investor?
faqs.a: No. It is a lien, and you can redeem it by paying the tax, interest and advertising cost. A tax deed application cannot come until two years have run.
